places.name: Hammerstein (Czarne)
places.what: Sally Leibholz born 1847. Georg born 1884 — which is why he cannot be Jacob’s brother

places.name: Szubin (Schubin)
places.what: Sally married Friederike 1874. Samuel 1877, Jacob 1884, Oskar 1887 all born here

places.name: Allenstein (Olsztyn)
places.what: Joachim Luwinski born 1865. A Landwirt

places.name: Sauerbaum (Zerbuń), Kreis Rössel
places.what: Johanna Thimm born 1871; Auguste born 1893

places.name: Berlin
places.what: Kurt born 1912. Four addresses: Meraner Str. 2, Kommandantenstr. 29, Waghäuseler Str. 9/10, Michaelkirchstr. 26

places.name: Sommerfeld
places.what: Where Siegfried was hidden, January 1943 to April 1945

places.name: Łódź
places.what: Georg and Lydia, in the ghetto from 1 November 1941

places.name: Chełmno (Kulmhof)
places.what: Georg and Lydia, 13 May 1942

places.name: Theresienstadt
places.what: Oskar, 17 March 1943

places.name: Auschwitz
places.what: Jacob 26 Feb 1943 · Samuel 10 Apr 1943 · Oskar 16 Oct 1944

places.name: Kraichtal
places.what: Auguste died 1975

places.name: Eixo, Aveiro
places.what: Augusto Pereira de Figueiredo baptised 1883 — candidate only

places.name: Porto
places.what: Ivone died and was buried

places.name: Amadora, Oeiras
places.what: Augusto died 21 August 1954

places.name: Lourenço Marques (Maputo)
places.what: Ivone Mota Figueiredo born 4 March 1922. Henrique born 1941

places.name: Johannesburg
places.what: The first document this archive holds placing Kurt in South Africa is his 1939 passport, issued at the German consulate here. The family tree says 1933 and a Berlin driving licence of 30 January 1934 says otherwise. Married 1948. Buried 1968 — Westpark, block L, grave 211

places.name: Santa Comba Dão, Viseu
places.what: Ivone's parents' home concelho — her father of the parish of VIMIEIRO, her mother of NEGOZELA. Named in her 1922 birth assento, read 27 September 2026.

places.name: Aldenham, Hertfordshire
places.what: Hawkins and Larkin. John Hawkins, baptised here in 1819, and Emma Larkin, baptised in 1822, had their banns called on 18 September 1842 and are at the Red Lion Cottages in 1871. Mary Appleyard and Mary Burch married into the parish, and their own baptisms have not been found.

places.name: Baldock, Hertfordshire
places.what: Martha Maud Castle’s family. She married Henry Robert Wear at the Congregational Church here on 31 October 1914.

places.name: Hitchin, Hertfordshire
places.what: The registration district of that marriage and of the births of the Wear children from 1917. Ada May Castle is Ada May Smith here in 1911, at 27 Churchyard.

places.name: Letchworth, Hertfordshire
places.what: The Wears at 72 Pix Road before they left for South Africa in 1937 and 1939. George William Castle, Martha Maud’s brother, lived at 85 Jackmans-place.

places.name: Bermondsey, London
places.what: William Wear, a harness maker, and Sarah Bloom, of Jamaica Road — whose line leads to Henry Robert Wear, born at St Olave, Bermondsey, in 1889 to Robert Wear and Emma Hawkins.

moves.note: The Leibholz move into the city.
The Luwinski move into the city.
Georg and Lydia. Deported to the Łódź ghetto on 1 November 1941 and murdered at Chełmno on 13 May 1942.
Oskar. Theresienstadt on 17 March 1943, Auschwitz nineteen months later on 16 October 1944.
Eight thousand kilometres south. The family tree dates it 1933; his Berlin driving licence is dated 30 January 1934, so the year is not established here. He lived.
How Ivone arrived, and the only reason these two halves are on one page.
Ivone at the end. Porto is a place nobody else in this archive ever saw.

moves.n: Santa Comba Dão to Lourenço Marques
moves.note: Joaquim Júlio de Figueiredo of Vimieiro and Leonia dos Santos Mata of Negozela, out to the colony before 1922 — the emigration the 'Repatriados' column implies and no passenger list has yet been found for.
The Dunvegan Castle, 10 August 1939, London to Durban, with Martha Maud Wear and four of her children. Britain declared war on 3 September.

note: Colours are this archive's own, read out of its Base.astro: --disp for Leibholz, --inf for Luwinski, --doc for Figueiredo, --accent for where it ended, --ink-faint for the 1933 crossing. The kit colours markers from JavaScript, so they are hex here rather than var() and DO NOT FOLLOW THE DARK THEME the way the hand-drawn SVG did. On the map that costs nothing - the tiles are light in both themes - which is why «both» is the mid tone --ink-soft and not --ink: a near-black dot was legible on the old drawing and would vanish from the legend on a dark page. The English line is a slate blue, #3b5b78, which is NOT a Base token: all five of Base’s accents were already taken.
